amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (20 مادة، بلا تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول) -- بعد الاطلاع على المعاملة الواردة من الديوان الملكي رقم 57511 وتاريخ 10/12/1438هـ المشتملة على خطاب المؤسسة العامة للموانئ رقم 01/3246 وتاريخ 10/7/1437هـ في شأن مشروع تنظيم الهيئة العامة للموانئ، وبعد الاطلاع على الفقرة (2) من المادة (24) من نظام مجلس الوزراء الصادر بالأمر الملكي رقم (أ/13) وتاريخ 3/3/1414هـ، وعلى الأمر الملكي رقم (55685) وتاريخ 30/11/1438هـ، وعلى نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/13) وتاريخ 7/4/1397هـ، وعلى نظام رسوم وأجور خدمات الموانئ الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/42) وتاريخ 2/7/1405هـ والمعدل بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/28) وتاريخ 19/9/1412هـ، وعلى المحضرين رقم (1199) ورقم (1200) المؤرخين في 24/9/1438هـ، والمذكرات رقم (1386) وتاريخ 24/11/1438هـ ورقم (491) وتاريخ 24/4/1439هـ ورقم (734) وتاريخ 11/6/1439هـ المعدة في هيئة الخبراء بمجلس الوزراء، وعلى توصيات مجلس الشؤون الاقتصادية والتنمية أرقام (1-63/38/د) و(26-27/38/د) و(21-6/39/د) و(18-22/39/د)، وعلى توصية اللجنة العامة لمجلس الوزراء رقم (2629) وتاريخ 11/6/1439هـ -- قرر مجلس الوزراء: أولاً- تعديل اسم (المؤسسة العامة للموانئ) ليكون (الهيئة العامة للموانئ). ثانياً- الموافقة على تنظيم الهيئة العامة للموانئ بالصيغة المرافقة. ثالثاً- اتفاق وزيري المالية والنقل على آليات استفادة الهيئة من إيرادات محددة خلال أول خمس سنوات من نفاذ التنظيم. رابعاً- أيلولة جميع حقوق وأموال والتزامات المؤسسة العامة للموانئ إلى الهيئة العامة للموانئ. خامساً- تكليف مجلس إدارة الهيئة بمعالجة عقود الإسناد القائمة. سادساً- تشكيل لجنة فنية لمعالجة وضع منسوبي المؤسسة العامة للموانئ. لم يُعثر هذه الجولة على أي قرار لاحق يعدّل مواد هذا التنظيم -- nezams.com's own metadata states 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (see mawani_no_amendments_single_source_negative_finding).

chapter_structure.label_ar: بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول
chapter_structure.title_ar: مواد متسلسلة غير مجمعة تحت أبواب أو فصول رسمية، لا يحمل أي منها عنواناً فرعياً في المصدر: التعريفات (م1) -- الشخصية الاعتبارية للهيئة ومقرها (م2) -- أهداف الهيئة واختصاصاتها (17 اختصاصاً) (م3) -- الأسس والمعايير التجارية لعمل الهيئة (م4) -- تشكيل مجلس الإدارة (م5) -- اجتماعات المجلس وقراراته (م6) -- اختصاصات المجلس (19 اختصاصاً) (م7) -- تعيين رئيس الهيئة واختصاصاته (م8) -- مديرو الموانئ (م9) -- المجالس الاستشارية للموانئ (م10) -- لائحة منح التراخيص (م11) -- موارد الهيئة (م12) -- إيداع أموال الهيئة (م13) -- ميزانية الهيئة والسنة المالية (م14) -- الإعفاءات والمزايا (م15) -- مراجع الحسابات الخارجي ورقابة ديوان المراقبة العامة (م16) -- التقرير السنوي (م17) -- خضوع منسوبي الهيئة لنظامي العمل والتأمينات الاجتماعية (م18) -- إحلال التنظيم محل نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ والإلغاء (م19) -- النشر والنفاذ (م20).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS THIS PASS: laws.boe.gov.sa's live portal was attempted directly against BOTH the exact LawDetails URL given in this track's task brief (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/a04e017e-cefb-4939-973f-a9ee00ff5646/1) and its 'Viewer' URL variant (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/Viewer/9edb2337-52b7-44f4-9750-a9ee00ff564f?lawId=a04e017e-cefb-4939-973f-a9ee00ff5646), via WebFetch and via three separate direct curl attempts (including one forcing TLS 1.2). WebFetch returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable on the LawDetails URL; every direct curl attempt against either URL returned 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' -- a TLS connection reset during the handshake itself, confirmed via curl -v, not a mere timeout or a proxy-side denial. This is consistent with this corpus's established reachability pattern for laws.boe.gov.sa in other tracks. A r.jina.ai reader-proxy fetch of the same LawDetails URL was also attempted and returned HTTP 422 (Playwright navigation timeout waiting for networkidle) -- also unsuccessful.

WAYBACK MACHINE CONFIRMED BLOCKED THIS PASS (unlike a prior sibling-track pass that could reach it): a WebFetch call to the Wayback CDX API for this exact BOE law ID returned the tool-level refusal 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org'; a second WebFetch attempt against a direct 'https://web.archive.org/web/2023/<BOE LawDetails URL>' snapshot URL returned the identical refusal. Direct curl to the same CDX endpoint over the pre-configured proxy returned 'Blocked by egress policy'. All three routes to the Wayback Machine are therefore confirmed closed this pass, not merely unattempted.

MAWANI'S OWN OFFICIAL SITE (mawani.gov.sa) CONFIRMED BLOCKED: direct curl (with a standard browser User-Agent) to both https://mawani.gov.sa and https://www.mawani.gov.sa/ar returned HTTP 405, serving an Alibaba Cloud WAF error page -- a confirmed block, not an omission. No official PDF of this statute was located on Mawani's own domain as a result.

UMM AL-QURA GAZETTE (uqn.gov.sa): the site's own root is reachable (HTTP 200, redirecting to www.uqn.gov.sa) but the specific gazette issue publishing Council of Ministers Resolution No. 299 (11/6/1439H) was NOT located within this pass's time budget -- a guessed search endpoint (/search.php) returned HTTP 404, and the site's own issue-by-issue archive navigation was not resolved to the specific issue this pass. This is flagged as an avenue for a future pass to strengthen this track's tier further, not silently omitted.

QANOONSA.COM: searched multiple ways this pass -- a direct site search for 'الهيئة العامة للموانئ', a WebSearch 'site:qanoonsa.com' query for the topic, and a further WebSearch for the resolution number (299) -- none surfaced a dedicated qanoonsa.com page reproducing this statute's text (only unrelated ports-sector decrees from other years were returned). This is a confirmed negative search result; qanoonsa.com's coverage does not appear to extend back to reproduce this specific 2018 decree, or it is simply not indexed there. mohamah.net was also searched and found to carry a page reproducing the PREDECESSOR statute (نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ السعودية, Royal Decree M/13, 7/4/1397H) but no page for the CURRENT (2018) Mawani organizational statute itself.

SINGLE FULL-TEXT SOURCE ACTUALLY REACHED -- nezams.com: fetched successfully via direct curl (browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, https://nezams.com/تنظيم-الهيئة-العامة-للموانئ/) after an earlier WebFetch call against the same URL returned only an AI-summarized paraphrase rather than verbatim text (that summary is NOT relied on anywhere in this track; only the raw HTML fetched directly via curl was used, parsed programmatically article-by-article from its own 'subject-N' HTML list structure). This yielded the complete text of all 20 articles, the decree number/date, and the site's own metadata field stating 'التعديلات: لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendments have been made to it). This is the ONLY full-text source this track was able to reach -- no second independent full-text mirror of this statute's article text was found despite extensive searching (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key mawani_single_fulltext_source_no_second_mirror_found). Given this corpus's strict 4-tier verification taxonomy (see scripts/gen_corpus_verification_tiers.py), this track is honestly classified as TIER_4_SINGLE_SOURCE_OR_MIXED_CONFIDENCE: exactly one source (a non-governmental secondary aggregator) was reached for the statute's actual article text, with the primary official channel (BOE) and its usual Wayback fallback both confirmed unreachable this pass, and no second independent full-text secondary source located.

INDEPENDENT METADATA-LEVEL (NOT FULL-TEXT) CORROBORATION: numerous independent web sources -- ar.wikipedia.org's article on the Authority, saudipedia.com's encyclopedia entry, my.gov.sa's official government-agency directory entry, and WebSearch-aggregated snippets quoting BOE's own page title/summary -- all independently corroborate the decree number (299), the Hijri date (11/6/1439H, corresponding to 26-27 February 2018G), the name change from 'المؤسسة العامة للموانئ' (Public Ports Corporation) to 'الهيئة العامة للموانئ' (General Authority for Ports / Mawani), the board composition (Minister of Transport as chair plus eight further seats), and the statute's scope (all commercial sea ports excluding military ports and economic-city ports). This is genuine, multi-source corroboration of the statute's IDENTITY and STRUCTURE, but it is corroboration of METADATA and SUMMARY-LEVEL facts, not a second verbatim reproduction of the 20 articles' own exact wording -- this distinction is why this track is classified TIER_4 rather than TIER_3 (which this corpus's taxonomy reserves for 2+ independent FULL-TEXT secondary sources agreeing with each other) despite this metadata corroboration.

NO AMENDMENTS FOUND: nezams.com's own page metadata states 'لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it), and independent WebSearch queries specifically probing for any Council of Ministers resolution amending this statute's articles returned no results. All 20 articles are accordingly treated as أصلية (original) -- this is a confirmed absence of any located amendment, not an exhaustive guarantee that none exists (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key mawani_no_amendments_single_source_negative_finding).

GENUINE PREDECESSOR REPEAL CLAUSE CONFIRMED: Article 19 of the statute's own text reads, verbatim: 'يحل التنظيم محل نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/13) وتاريخ 7/4/1397هـ، ويُلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام.' ('This Statute replaces the Statute of the Public Ports Corporation, issued by Royal Decree No. M/13 dated 7/4/1397H, and repeals whatever conflicts with it.') This is an explicit, article-level repeal-and-replace clause naming a genuine predecessor instrument, not merely the enacting resolution's own separate naming decision (which is recorded distinctly in this track's preamble_ar/issuing_authority fields, per 'أولاً' of Resolution 299's own recital: 'تعديل اسم (المؤسسة العامة للموانئ) ليكون (الهيئة العامة للموانئ)').

STRUCTURE: flat sequence of 20 individually-numbered مواد, no أبواب/فصول subdivision, no inline per-article topic titles in the source (every heading is a bare ordinal followed only by the word 'المادة' + ordinal) -- no title_ar key is used, consistent with this corpus's rega_organizational_statute/cst_organizational_statute precedent for sources lacking inline per-article titles.

NORMALIZATION PERFORMED: Article 1's defined-term column uses decorative Arabic tatweel (kashida, U+0640) characters for visual letter-spacing/column-alignment in nezams.com's own HTML rendering (e.g. 'المـمـلكـة' for 'المملكة', 'الهــيئــة' for 'الهيئة'). These decorative tatweel runs were stripped as a pure typographic normalization -- carefully distinguished from the legitimate 'هـ' Hijri-date abbreviation and the 'هـ-' fifth-ordinal board-list letter used in Article 5, both of which were verified preserved intact (tatweel was only stripped where flanked by Arabic letters on BOTH sides, never at a word boundary). Zero-width non-joiner/joiner characters and non-breaking spaces present in the source HTML's markup (outside the article text) were likewise not carried into the ingested text. No other legal text is altered beyond this whitespace/decorative-character normalization. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English text in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en is for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: This track's actual article-level text rests on exactly ONE full-text source reached this pass: nezams.com. Despite extensive searching (direct site searches, WebSearch 'site:' filters, resolution-number searches, and targeted phrase searches for specific article sentences to locate any independent mirror), no second full-text reproduction of this statute's 20 articles was found on qanoonsa.com, qistas.com, mohamah.net, eastlaws.com, or any other secondary aggregator. mohamah.net carries a page for the PREDECESSOR statute only, not this one. This is why this track is classified TIER_4_SINGLE_SOURCE_OR_MIXED_CONFIDENCE rather than TIER_3 (which requires 2+ independent full-text secondary sources agreeing with each other) despite substantial independent metadata-level corroboration (decree number/date, name change, board composition, scope) from unrelated sources -- see verification_methodology_note.

laws.boe.gov.sa returned HTTP 503 (WebFetch) and a TLS connection reset during the handshake (three separate direct curl attempts, including a TLS-1.2-forced attempt) on both its LawDetails and Viewer URLs for this exact law. A r.jina.ai reader-proxy fetch also failed (HTTP 422, navigation timeout). The Wayback Machine was independently confirmed blocked via two separate WebFetch calls (both returned the tool-level refusal 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org') and via a direct curl to its CDX API ('Blocked by egress policy'). All primary-portal and Wayback-fallback routes are therefore confirmed closed this pass, not merely unattempted.

mawani.gov.sa (the Authority's own official website) returned HTTP 405 with an Alibaba Cloud WAF error page on direct curl to both its root and /ar path, using a standard browser User-Agent. No official PDF of this statute could be located on the Authority's own domain as a result -- a confirmed block, not an omission.

uqn.gov.sa (Umm Al-Qura Gazette) is itself reachable (HTTP 200 at its root, redirecting to www.uqn.gov.sa), but the specific gazette issue publishing Council of Ministers Resolution No. 299 (11/6/1439H) was not located within this pass's time budget -- a guessed search endpoint returned HTTP 404, and the site's own issue-archive navigation was not resolved to the specific issue. Flagged as an avenue for a future pass, not silently omitted.

nezams.com's own metadata for this law states 'التعديلات: لم يجرى عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it), and targeted WebSearch queries for any Council of Ministers resolution amending this statute's own articles returned no results. All 20 articles are accordingly treated as أصلية (original). This is a confirmed absence of any LOCATED amendment given the sources actually reached this pass -- not an exhaustive guarantee, verified against BOE itself, that none exists, since BOE was unreachable this pass (see mawani_boe_and_wayback_confirmed_unreachable_this_pass).

Article 19 of the statute's own text explicitly names and repeals its predecessor: 'يحل التنظيم محل نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/13) وتاريخ 7/4/1397هـ، ويُلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام.' This is a genuine, explicit, article-level repeal-and-replace clause naming a real predecessor instrument (the Statute of the Public Ports Corporation, Royal Decree M/13, 7/4/1397H) -- distinct from, and in addition to, the enacting Resolution 299's own separate naming decision (recorded in this track's preamble_ar) that merely renamed the entity from 'المؤسسة العامة للموانئ' to 'الهيئة العامة للموانئ' without itself being a repeal clause.

Article 8's list of the Authority President's powers ends numbered item 14 ('تمثيل الهيئة في علاقاتها مع الجهات الحكومية ومع الغير.'), immediately followed by a general delegation sentence ('وللرئيس تفويض من يراه من منسوبي الهيئة في بعض هذه الاختصاصات والمهمات.'), and ONLY THEN a further numbered item 15 ('تمثيل الهيئة أمام الجهات القضائية، وله تفويض من يراه في ذلك.'). This ordering -- a numbered list item appearing AFTER the article's own general closing/delegation sentence -- was verified twice against nezams.com's raw HTML and is reproduced exactly as found. This track cannot independently confirm, from a second source, whether this reflects the statute's original 2018 drafting (plausible, given nezams.com's own 'no amendments' metadata) or an unlogged later amendment appending item 15 -- it is preserved literally rather than silently reordered.

Article 5's board-composition list appends a role-designation word after each entry (e.g. 'رئيساً' for the chair, 'عضواً' -- singular 'member' -- for each single-person seat). The final entry (ز, three private-sector seats) closes with the PLURAL role-word 'أعضاء' ('members') rather than 'عضواً', preceded by a full stop: '... بناء على اقتراح من الوزير. أعضاء'. Close reading shows this is a grammatically consistent application of the same per-item role-labeling convention (singular label for a one-person seat, plural label for the three-person seat) rather than a transcription artifact -- but is flagged given this track's single-source reliance, since no second source was found to independently corroborate this exact placement/punctuation.

nezams.com's own HTML rendering of Article 1's defined-term column uses decorative Arabic tatweel (kashida) characters for visual letter-spacing (e.g. 'المـمـلكـة' for 'المملكة', 'الهــيئــة' for 'الهيئة', 'الـمجلس' for 'المجلس'). This track strips these decorative tatweel runs as a pure typographic/whitespace-equivalent normalization (consistent with this corpus's established rega_organizational_statute/cst_organizational_statute practice), carefully distinguished from -- and NOT applied to -- the legitimate 'هـ' Hijri-date abbreviation (Articles 7 and 19) and the 'هـ-' fifth-ordinal board-list letter (Article 5), both verified preserved intact. The underlying words are unchanged; only decorative characters are removed.

qanoonsa.com, used as a secondary cross-check source for several other tracks in this corpus, was searched multiple independent ways and no dedicated page reproducing this statute's text was found -- likely because qanoonsa.com's indexed coverage does not extend back to this 2018 decree, or the decree is simply not indexed there. mohamah.net carries a page for the statute's PREDECESSOR (نظام المؤسسة العامة للموانئ السعودية) only, confirming that instrument's own citation (Royal Decree M/13, 7/4/1397H) matches Article 19's own repeal clause, but does not provide a second source for the CURRENT statute's own article text. These are confirmed negative/partial search results, not omissions.
